title: A uniform introduction rule for intuitionistic primitive recursive arithmetic

new_theory.name: R, the root-dependent uniform-introduction orbit calculus
new_theory.numerical_terms: variables, zero, successor, scalar iterator I(n,a;u.h)
new_theory.formula_grammar: equations, Q_y B, D_x,y B; unrestricted
claims: admissible numerical substitution by direct induction on derivations
explicit derivation-preserving translations in both directions with the pinned native calculus
both formula round trips for the whole public language
whole numerical domains with actual equality and identity numerical composites
bi-interpretability and equiconsistency with full first-order iPRA by composition with the inherited bridge
new_theory.proof_status: Written metatheoretic proofs; not newly verified by Lean or Rocq

simplicity.primary_contract: Complete standalone typed JSON checkers with matched public-grammar, scoping, and substitution validation
simplicity.normalization: Remove genuine docstrings; ast.unparse plus one LF; entire standalone module

ancillary.theory: Earlier guarded-source calculus, not the new R calculus
ancillary.change_type: Implementation composition, not a new axiomatization
ancillary.public_input_contract: Inherited canonical guarded public goals; compact modules are not complete canonical public-grammar validators

verification.scope: Finite executable controls, not a proof-assistant verification of the metatheorems.

limitations: Finite checker controls are not metatheorem proofs.
The new orbit calculus does not minimize all measured implementation coordinates.
No absolute meaning of smallest independent of syntax and cost model is established.
